title: Nightly stock check, line by line
subtitle: One run over 40 products: load the stock file, work out what each needs, group orders by supplier, write them out.

reorder.py:2.title: Import from the standard library
reorder.py:2.text: csv for parsing the stock file, json for writing the orders, sys for the optional path argument, and dataclass to generate Item's __init__ and __repr__ from its annotated fields.

reorder.py:7.title: Define the reorder policy
reorder.py:7.text: SAFETY_DAYS is how many days of sales to keep on hand, MIN_ORDER the smallest quantity worth ordering. Both are read by needed() for every product.

reorder.py:13.title: Define the Item record and the functions
reorder.py:13.text: @dataclass turns the four annotated class attributes into constructor parameters, so Item(sku, on_hand, daily_sales, supplier) works without a hand-written __init__. The annotations are not enforced: the conversion to int and float happens in load().

reorder.py:49.title: Run main() when executed as a script
reorder.py:49.text: sys.argv[1:] is unpacked into main(), so an optional first argument replaces the default STOCK_CSV path.

reorder.py:42.title: Load the stock file
reorder.py:42.text: Calls load() and binds the list of Item records it returns.

reorder.py:22.title: Open the CSV for reading
reorder.py:22.text: newline="" is what the csv module expects: it lets the reader handle line endings itself, including newlines inside quoted fields.

reorder.py:23.title: Parse every row into an Item
reorder.py:23.text: csv.DictReader yields one dict per row keyed by the header line. The list comprehension converts on_hand to int and daily_sales to float, because the reader returns strings. The whole file is read before the with block closes it: 40 items.

reorder.py:43.title: Plan the orders
reorder.py:43.text: Hands the items to plan_orders(), which returns a dict mapping each supplier to its order lines.

reorder.py:33.title: Start an empty order book
reorder.py:33.text: Keys will be supplier names, values lists of order lines; suppliers only appear once something is ordered from them.

reorder.py:34.title: Check every product
reorder.py:34.text: One iteration per Item; the loop body asks needed() for a quantity and records it if it's non-zero. It ran 40 times, once per product in the file.

reorder.py:35.title: Work out how much to order
reorder.py:35.text: Calls needed() for the current item; 0 means no order.

reorder.py:27.title: Compute the stock to keep on hand
reorder.py:27.text: Target stock is a week of sales: daily_sales times SAFETY_DAYS. It's a float, since sales are averages.

reorder.py:28.title: Compute the shortfall
reorder.py:28.text: How far stock on hand is below the target. Negative means there is more than enough.

reorder.py:29.title: Round up to a sensible order
reorder.py:29.text: A conditional expression: no shortfall gives 0. Otherwise the shortfall is rounded and raised to at least MIN_ORDER. Note that round() uses banker's rounding, so a shortfall of 12.5 orders 12, not 13.

reorder.py:36.title: Only record items that need ordering
reorder.py:36.text: 0 is falsy, so items with enough stock are skipped without an explicit comparison.

reorder.py:37.title: Add the order line under its supplier
reorder.py:37.text: setdefault returns the supplier's existing list, or inserts and returns a new empty one, so the first order for a supplier needs no special case.

reorder.py:38.title: Return the order book
reorder.py:38.text: 16 order lines across 3 suppliers: Acme 6, Borealis 8, Cobalt 2.

reorder.py:44.title: Write the orders as JSON
reorder.py:44.text: Opening with "w" truncates any previous orders.json. In safe mode codestory redirected the file to its sandbox, so the real file was not touched.

reorder.py:45.title: Serialise the order book
reorder.py:45.text: json.dump writes the dict straight to the file handle; indent=2 makes it readable for whoever places the orders.

notes.s18: First product, SKU-100: a week of sales is 38.5 units, and with 159 on hand the shortfall is -120.5, so nothing is ordered.
